messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated 5xx and upstream timeouts observed for gateway-prod. paging oncall. scope: /api/v1/generate, ~12% 5xx, spikes since ~00:40 UTC. sampling=1/1000.

james: seeing the spike on dashboards. 5xx is mostly 502/504 from the gateway returning upstream errors. customer-facing errors up ~8%. rolling alerts from latency and error-rate.

maya: are there any recent deploys to edge or gateway?

james: not in the last 3 hours. deploy-bot shows last deploy to gateway was ~6h ago.

ops-runbook-bot: runbook: gateway-5xx -> check kvcache, connection pool, mesos/gpu autoscale, and upstream model endpoints.

leo: quick check: kv cache hit rate dropped from 78% -> 31% around 00:38. could be cache invalidation storm.

sara: logs show a lot of errors without request_id header. traces are sparse — sampling probably too low or trace headers not propagated.

james: yeah that matches. most error logs look like this:```\nERROR gateway: upstream timeout (context cancelled)\npath=/api/v1/generate host=gateway-prod pod=gw-32\nerror=timeout upstream=10.0.12.45:8080\n```\nno span id, no request_id.

maya: customer impact: a handful of high-traffic customers seeing timeouts on LLM calls; some retries causing higher load. working with support to flag customer tickets.

james: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) increase trace sampling and enable lightweight req_id logging in gateway (stopgap) 2) temporarily route a fraction of traffic to fallback model variant with lower latency 3) scale gateway pool and upstream pools 4) if cache is the cause, disable aggressive invalidation.

leo: I can flip a quick release to add request_id header logging (very small change). patch would add `X-Request-Id` to structured logs and emit at info for 1 hour. low-risk.

sara: we need more traces to diagnose root cause. current sampling=1/1000 — propose 1/50 for 30 mins, then revert. that should help correlate client->upstream failures. ops-runbook-bot suggests toggling APM sampling via console.

james: doing the sampling ramp now (console: tracing.sampling.gateway=0.02). also bumping gateway log level for http handlers to INFO for 10m.

on-deploy-bot: patch scheduled: gw-add-reqid-logs -> rolling restart gw-* (3m per pod). triggered by james.

maya: while we have limited traces, do we have any telemetry that ties affected requests to a particular upstream (model host pool)?

leo: preliminary: the backend pool region-us-east-2-instance-set-B shows increased queue depth and connection resets. pushing more capacity there now.

james: scaled upstream pool +2 nodes (manual). watching 5xx. initial drop from 12% -> 7%.

support-notify: sent message to affected customers with workarounds (retries/backoff) and ETA copy.

maya: handoff plan: james (current oncall) -> maya (secondary) at :10. james to document actions taken. need to confirm if stopgap logging captured request_ids.

james: documenting summary in incident doc. key actions so far: increased trace sampling, added temporary request_id logs, scaled upstream pool, temporary config to relax cache invalidation.

sara: quick check of logs post-reqid patch: we now have request ids in ~95% of new logs. example:```\nINFO gateway: request start path=/api/v1/generate request_id=rid_abc123 client=svc-xyz\nINFO proxy: upstream call start request_id=rid_abc123 upstream=10.0.12.45:8080\nERROR proxy: upstream timeout request_id=rid_abc123 upstream_error=timeout\n```\nthis lets us correlate to specific upstream hosts.

james: good. next diagnostic: look at connection reset traces for rid_* and map to instance set.

leo: extracted small sample: connection resets coincide with short-lived CPU spikes on host 10.0.12.45 and large batch sizes arriving. kernel stomping ephemeral ports? not sure yet.

maya: while you dig deeper, we should put a stopgap routing rule to send 25% of traffic to warm-fallback cluster (lower concurrency config) to reduce pressure. that should reduce 5xx quickly.

james: applying routing override now (route policy: fallback-25pct).

ops-runbook-bot: mitigation checklist item: announce pager update -> done. update customer-impact doc -> pending.

sara: note — traces still missing for a subset of requests even after sampling increase. investigating header propagation issues at the LB. could be that health proxy strips trace header when retrying.

leo: interesting — ingress proxy config shows `proxy_set_header` for trace headers, but our retry proxy (edge-retry) does a raw proxy without copying all headers for rewrites. we can flip a config flag `preserve_trace_headers=true` as an immediate stopgap. low-risk but requires a rolling restart of edge-retry.

maya: do it. we'll coordinate restarts during low-traffic windows but now priority is visibility.

james: scheduled edge-retry restart (strategy: sequential, 2m grace). going to bump maintenance window flags.

non-deploy-bot: edge-retry-config-change -> flagging for audit.

james: after routing + scale + reqid + header-preserve, 5xx is down to ~3.5% and customer impact reduced to ~2% of calls failing. still watching.

maya: handoff now. james please paste a short runbook and current hypothesis. i'll pick this up and keep monitoring + liaise with support for customer comms.

james: handoff notes:\n- hypothesis: upstream instance set B overloaded by burst of large batch requests combined with cache churn; some requests retried by edge-retry losing trace headers -> sparse traces.\n- actions taken: increased tracing sampling (1/50), added X-Request-Id logs, scaled upstream pool +2 nodes, routing override to fallback-25pct, enabled preserve_trace_headers on edge-retry, relaxed cache invalidation rule.\n- next steps for oncall: continue to monitor 5xx and traces, collect correlated traces for sample request_ids, check host 10.0.12.45 for kernel/retry metrics, consider circuit-breaker for B pool if errors persist.

maya: ack. I will: 1) pull a 1-hour trace sample and correlate host CPU/network metrics; 2) schedule a deeper config review with infra for cache invalidation rules tomorrow; 3) validate rollback plan for routing override.

ops-runbook-bot: incident severity -> S2 (customer-impacting, partial degradation). escalate to eng-runtime if 5xx > 5% sustained for > 15m.

james: leaving thread. if anything spikes, ping me DM.

maya: will monitor. good job on quick instrumentation. next engineering follow-up: adopt permanent lightweight req_id propagation and add a small always-on trace sampling (0.5%) for production to avoid blindspots during incidents.

sara: filing follow-up tickets: INFRA-4532 (permanent req_id propagation), RTL-772 (trace sampling policy), OBS-9901 (edge-retry header audit).

leo: adding note to playbook: "when traces sparse -> increase sampling and preserve trace headers before scaling".

on-deploy-bot: incident closed to active mitigation phase. moving to monitoring.

james: thanks team.

maya: closing handoff. I'll update incident timeline and customer summary in the incident board.
